title: How can the sheet add a whole row of marks?
description: The six marks of the second student sit in one row of the sheet. The video adds them by hand and then writes the formula that makes the sheet do it. Keeko picks only the first and last cells and is corrected.
teaching_notes: One idea: the formula SUM over a range adds every cell from the first to the last, and the colon is what makes it a range. Watch for students who separate the first and last cells with a comma and add only two cells.

source: Nagesh's marks are 41, 43, 48, 39, 34 and 39. Find his total, and say the formula.
video_script.why: A child who can name a row of cells as a range now uses that range inside a formula that adds the whole row.
video_script.substitution: the book's marks of Nagesh in B3:G3: 41, 43, 48, 39, 34, 39
video_script.anchor: the marks sheet with the second student row B3:G3 lit and the six marks written in it
video_script.wrong_move: types =SUM(B3,G3) with a comma, which adds only the first cell and the last cell, 41 + 39 = 80; the colon in B3:G3 makes the range that adds all six
video_script.payoff_line: The total is two hundred and forty four, from equals sum of B three to G three

final_answer.spoken: the total is two hundred and forty four, from equals sum of B three to G three

maths_rules: check: six marks each near 40 give about 6 × 40 = 240, close to 244
formula: =SUM(B3:G3); the colon makes the range, so all six cells are added
slip: =SUM(B3,G3) adds only B3 and G3, 41 + 39 = 80
video_script.design: One marks sheet all video. The six marks are added in pairs, then the formula is built from an equals sign, the word sum and the range. Keeko types a comma and the bubble is struck out.
open_questions: The worklist answer is 250 because it lists the fifth mark as 40. The book row for Nagesh is 41, 43, 48, 39, 34, 39, which totals 244. This script uses 244; please confirm against the printed sheet.

marks.move: an arrow in the bubble points at the comma between B3 and G3

marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the colon makes all six cells light up

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the total is eighty.
<bookmark mark='move'/>Keeko typed the first cell and the last cell with a comma between them.
<bookmark mark='why'/>A comma picks only those two cells. Forty one plus thirty nine is eighty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A colon picks every cell from B three to G three, so all six marks are added.
